happy_path.title: Manual podcast trigger with a valid slug logs the slug as a %s argument and returns an execution
happy_path.preconditions: Precondition: S1 and S3 passed. Blocked until PR #100 (8b5eb66) is deployed to integ (comment 346733).
steps: GET {base}/api/cron/schedules with the S1 token and note one schedule slug from the response.
POST {base}/api/cron/trigger/{slug} with the S1 token, Content-Type application/json and body {"variables":{}}.
Record the HTTP status and body.
In the API pod logs, find the line for this request.
happy_path.expected: The log contains exactly one line `[CRON-API] 🎯 Manual trigger: <slug>`, with the slug written as sent. The response is a success and its body includes `execution.id`. Record the exact status. Neither a 5xx nor the handler's 400 'Failed to trigger podcast generation' is a pass.

edge_cases.title: Unknown slug containing format specifiers: rejected, and the failure log prints the slug literally next to the error
edge_cases.preconditions: Precondition: S1 and S3 passed. Blocked until PR #100 (8b5eb66) is deployed.
steps: POST {base}/api/cron/trigger/qa-%25s-%25d with the S1 token and body {"variables":{}}.
Record the status, the body, and which layer answered.
If the handler answered, find the '[CRON-API] ❌ Manual trigger failed for' line in the API logs.
edge_cases.expected: The request is rejected with no podcast generated, and any 4xx passes; record the status and which layer answered (rule AC: the CDN, ingress or router may handle a percent-encoded path first). If the handler answered (body error 'Failed to trigger podcast generation'), the log line reads `[CRON-API] ❌ Manual trigger failed for qa-%s-%d:` with the slug literal and the error printed after it, not substituted into the slug.
